appliedUpdates.description: Updated cleanup-notes.md: clarified that SSE quat module is live code (re-exported via pub use crate::sse::quat::Quat on x86/x86_64), not dead code. Previous note said 'verify before removing' which could mislead future workers.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add a note about module inlining as an alternative to deletion when a module is a thin wrapper around a single item. The skill currently says 'If removing a file, also remove its mod declaration in the parent' but doesn't cover the case where a module contains useful code that should be moved rather than deleted. Example: entities/ module contained only Camera re-exported via mod.rs - worker correctly inlined camera.rs into application/camera.rs and updated all import paths.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: dead-code-cleanup worker session: entities/ directory contained only Camera struct in camera.rs re-exported via mod.rs. Worker moved camera.rs to application/ and updated 2 import paths. Skill procedure only mentions deletion, not inlining.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add guidance about when targeted #[allow(dead_code)] is acceptable. Current rules don't distinguish between dead code that's truly obsolete vs dead code that's part of planned-but-unimplemented features. Suggested rule: #[allow(dead_code)] is acceptable for: (1) GPU buffer layout structs where fields are only written, never read by Rust code, (2) fields/types that are part of planned features with clear implementation intent documented. NOT acceptable for: code that appears abandoned or has no clear future use.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: dead-code-cleanup worker correctly added targeted #[allow(dead_code)] to SkeletalAnimationSystem.sample_buffer (planned feature) and GPU layout structs in storage_uniform.rs (FrameUniforms/ObjectUniforms fields only written to GPU). Both are justified but the decision framework isn't documented.
